passages.p1:
Exams have been a part of school life for hundreds of years, and today they remain one of the most common ways to measure learning. In simple terms, an exam is a test that asks students to show what they know and can do within a fixed time. Schools and universities use exams to decide grades, to compare students, and to choose who can move on to the next level of study. Because so many important decisions depend on them, exams are taken seriously by students, parents, and teachers alike. Yet people still argue about whether these tests are truly the best way to judge a young person's ability.

For many students, exams provide a clear goal to work towards. Knowing that a test is coming can push learners to review their notes, organise their time, and study material they might otherwise ignore. In this way, exams can increase motivation and encourage good study habits. However, the same pressure can also cause problems. Some students feel so worried about failing that they cannot sleep or concentrate, and a few perform far below their real level on the day. This kind of stress does not affect everyone equally; while certain learners enjoy the challenge, others find that fear gets in the way of clear thinking.

Exams are useful for teachers as well as students. When a class sits a test, the results show which topics have been understood and which need more attention. A teacher might notice, for example, that most students did well in grammar but struggled with reading. Such information helps teachers adjust their lessons and plan better for the future. In this sense, an exam is not only a judgement of students but also a mirror that reflects the quality of the teaching itself.

Despite these benefits, many people warn against relying on exams too heavily. One common criticism is that a single test only captures a small part of what a student can do. Skills such as creativity, teamwork, and speaking are difficult to measure in a written paper, yet they matter greatly in real life. Critics also point out that some learners are simply better at taking tests than others, which means high marks do not always reflect deep understanding. When schools focus only on exam results, teachers may end up teaching to the test rather than helping students think for themselves.

Most educators today therefore support a balanced approach. Exams still have an important role to play, but they work best alongside other methods such as projects, presentations, and continuous classroom assessment. Used wisely, tests can guide both learning and teaching without becoming a source of unnecessary fear. The goal, after all, is not to produce students who are good at exams, but to help them become confident, capable people who are ready for the challenges beyond the classroom.
passages.p2:
For most of human history, the word 'milk' has referred to a liquid produced by mammals, above all the cow. In recent years, however, food scientists have begun to look elsewhere, and one of their more surprising experiments is a product that has been nicknamed 'fish milk'. Despite its name, fish milk is not drawn from any animal in the way dairy is. Instead, it is a beverage engineered from proteins and oils extracted from fish or fish by-products, then blended with water and other ingredients until it resembles ordinary milk in colour and texture. Researchers argue that such alternatives deserve serious attention, not as a novelty, but as a possible answer to pressing problems in nutrition and the environment.

The production process is more complex than it first appears. Manufacturers usually begin with parts of the fish that would otherwise be discarded, such as the trimmings left over after fillets are cut. These are carefully cleaned and treated to remove the strong smell and flavour that most consumers associate with seafood. The remaining proteins and healthy fats are then separated and recombined with water, natural sweeteners and stabilisers. Because the raw material is often waste from the fishing industry, supporters claim that the method turns a disposal problem into a valuable food, reducing the amount of edible matter that ends up as rubbish.

The motives behind this research are varied. One is the environmental cost of dairy farming, which uses large areas of land and releases significant quantities of greenhouse gases. Another is health: a considerable share of the world's population cannot digest lactose, the sugar found in cow's milk, and therefore avoids dairy altogether. Fish milk contains no lactose, and it is naturally rich in omega-3 fatty acids, nutrients linked to heart and brain health that are scarce in many modern diets. For scientists, a drink that is sustainable, lactose-free and nutritious at the same time is an attractive prospect.

Early studies have produced encouraging but mixed results. Laboratory tests confirm that the protein content of fish milk can match or even exceed that of dairy, and that its fats remain stable during storage. The main obstacle, unsurprisingly, is taste. In consumer trials, some participants reported a faint fishy aftertaste that they found off-putting, while others could not tell the difference once the drink was flavoured. Persuading shoppers to accept a milk made from fish, researchers admit, may prove harder than solving the technical difficulties. Clever marketing and familiar flavours such as vanilla or chocolate are being tested as ways to overcome this resistance.

If these hurdles can be cleared, the possible applications are wide-ranging. Fish milk could be used not only as a drink but also as an ingredient in yoghurts, sauces and baked goods, or as a fortified supplement for people who lack omega-3 in their diets. Some developers even imagine it playing a role in regions where fresh dairy is difficult to store or transport. Whether or not it ever reaches supermarket shelves in large quantities, the research reflects a broader shift in thinking: that the food of the future may come from sources we have long overlooked.
passages.p3:
The rapid integration of digital technology into classrooms has provoked one of the liveliest debates in contemporary education. Enthusiasts hail it as a long-overdue revolution, while sceptics warn against overstating its promise. A more measured appraisal, however, reveals that the influence of digital tools is neither uniformly positive nor negative; rather, it reshapes learning along several distinct dimensions—the quality of what students learn, the methods by which they are taught, the costs involved, and the very nature of educational employment. Weighing these dimensions against one another is essential to understanding what technology genuinely offers.

The most frequently cited benefit concerns the quality of learning. Adaptive software can tailor exercises to an individual's pace, dwelling on concepts a learner finds difficult and accelerating past those already mastered. Such personalisation was once the privilege of students who could afford private tuition; now it is embedded in inexpensive applications. Equally valuable is the instantaneous feedback these systems provide. Where a teacher marking thirty essays might take a week to return them, an algorithm can flag errors within seconds, allowing misconceptions to be corrected before they harden into habits. Some platforms go further still, compiling dashboards that reveal at a glance which topics a whole cohort has yet to grasp—information that would otherwise remain buried in a pile of marked papers.

Digital tools have also transformed the methods of instruction. Online courses dissolve the barriers of distance, granting learners in remote areas access to lectures once confined to elite campuses. Blended models, which interleave face-to-face sessions with digital content, have become commonplace, while the so-called flipped classroom inverts the traditional order altogether: students absorb new material at home through recorded lessons and reserve class time for discussion and problem-solving. This rearrangement frees the teacher from the role of mere lecturer, transforming them into a guide who intervenes precisely where confusion arises. Crucially, these arrangements do not require every school to abandon its lecture halls overnight; the more thoughtful adopters retain whatever genuinely serves their pupils and discard only what technology can plainly improve upon.

On the question of cost, the picture is more ambivalent. Proponents point out that digital textbooks and open educational resources can be duplicated at almost no expense, sparing families the recurrent burden of buying printed volumes. Yet this apparent thrift conceals a substantial outlay. Reliable devices, robust networks and continual software updates demand considerable capital, and institutions in less affluent regions frequently struggle to furnish them. The consequence is a paradox: a technology celebrated for widening access may, if unevenly distributed, deepen the very divide it was meant to bridge.

The impact on employment is perhaps the most contentious dimension. Automation has spawned entirely new occupations—instructional designers, learning analysts and educational technologists—that scarcely existed a generation ago. At the same time, veteran teachers are being urged to acquire fresh competencies, from managing virtual platforms to interpreting performance data. Not everyone welcomes this pressure, and some fear that routine tasks, and even a portion of teaching itself, may eventually be delegated to machines. Whether such displacement materialises on any significant scale remains uncertain, but the anxiety it generates is real.

Taken together, these considerations caution against sweeping verdicts. Digital technology can undoubtedly enrich learning, diversify methods and, under the right conditions, economise on resources. Yet its benefits are contingent rather than automatic, dependent on thoughtful investment, equitable access and a workforce prepared to adapt. The wisest course, then, is neither uncritical enthusiasm nor reflexive resistance, but a discerning readiness to harness what works while remaining alert to what it may quietly cost. History, after all, is littered with innovations that dazzled at first yet delivered far less than they seemed to promise, and education can ill afford to repeat that pattern.
passages.p4:
The United States dollar occupies a position in the world economy that is difficult to overstate. Beyond serving as the domestic currency of a single nation, it functions as the principal medium through which international commerce is conducted and the leading store of value in which central banks hold their reserves. When a Brazilian exporter sells soybeans to a buyer in Indonesia, the transaction is very often settled not in either party's home currency but in dollars. This arrangement, sometimes described as the dollar's 'exorbitant privilege,' allows the United States to borrow abroad cheaply and grants Washington a degree of financial leverage that no other government enjoys.

Several factors explain why so many countries gravitate towards the dollar. The first is trust: the American economy is large, its institutions are relatively transparent, and its government has never defaulted on its obligations. The second is liquidity, for the markets in dollar-denominated assets are so deep that vast sums can be bought or sold without moving prices sharply. A third factor is inertia, or what economists call a network effect: because everyone else uses dollars, using anything else becomes inconvenient. Together these forces entrench the currency's supremacy even as America's share of global output gradually declines.

The value of the dollar, however, is far from fixed, and its fluctuations ripple outward with considerable force. When the dollar weakens, or depreciates, against other currencies, American-made goods become cheaper for foreign buyers, which tends to stimulate exports and, over time, narrow the trade deficit. Yet the same movement makes imported goods dearer for American consumers, feeding domestic inflation. For the rest of the world the picture inverts: countries that sell to the United States find their products less competitive, while commodities priced in dollars, such as oil and metals, appear cheaper to buyers holding stronger currencies.

A strengthening, or appreciating, dollar produces the opposite and frequently more painful consequences abroad. Because many developing nations borrow in dollars rather than in their own currencies, a rising dollar inflates the real burden of their debts almost overnight; a loan that once seemed manageable becomes crushing when each dollar of repayment costs more in local money. At the same time, imported commodities grow costlier, straining economies that depend on foreign oil or food. Capital, meanwhile, tends to flow towards the United States in search of higher returns, draining funds from emerging markets precisely when they can least afford it.

This asymmetry lies at the heart of longstanding complaints about the dollar-centred system. Critics argue that decisions taken in Washington—above all by the Federal Reserve when it raises or lowers interest rates—are transmitted to every corner of the globe, whether or not local conditions warrant such a shock. A poor harvest or a political crisis in a small economy can be dwarfed, in its effect on ordinary lives, by a shift in American monetary policy over which that economy has no say whatsoever. For this reason some governments have quietly sought to diversify, holding a portion of their reserves in euros, gold, or, more recently, the Chinese renminbi.

Yet talk of the dollar's imminent demise has been circulating for decades, and it remains, for now, largely premature. No rival currency combines the depth, safety, and universal acceptance that the dollar offers, and the very habit of using it perpetuates its dominance. What is clear is that so long as the world's trade and debt are denominated in dollars, the fortunes of distant economies will remain tightly bound to the value of a currency they neither issue nor control—a dependence that is at once a convenience and a vulnerability.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The history of examinations in universities around the world.
B. The best techniques that students can use to pass difficult exams.
C. The value of exams and the debate over how much to depend on them.
D. The reasons why students feel stressed before important tests.
questions.explanation: Cả bài vừa nêu lợi ích của kỳ thi (đoạn 2,3) vừa nêu tranh luận và cách tiếp cận cân bằng (đoạn 4,5), nên ý chính là giá trị của kỳ thi và tranh luận về mức độ dựa vào chúng → C. A (lịch sử) và D (căng thẳng) chỉ là chi tiết nhỏ, không bao trùm; B (kỹ thuật thi) không được bàn tới.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

Why do schools and universities give exams, according to paragraph 1?
options: A. To replace the need for teachers in the classroom.
B. To set grades and decide who can continue studying.
C. To reduce the pressure that parents place on children.
D. To make lessons shorter and easier to plan.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1 nói trường dùng kỳ thi để 'decide grades... choose who can move on to the next level' → B là cách diễn đạt lại đúng. A và D không được nhắc; C trái nội dung (kỳ thi thường tạo áp lực chứ không giảm).

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 2, one positive effect of exams is that they
options: A. remove all worry from the learning process.
B. guarantee that every student sleeps well before a test.
C. make regular studying completely unnecessary.
D. encourage learners to plan their time and revise.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: kỳ thi thúc đẩy người học 'review their notes, organise their time' → D. A và B trái ý (đoạn nói áp lực còn gây mất ngủ, lo lắng); C sai vì kỳ thi khuyến khích học, không loại bỏ việc học.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What does paragraph 2 say about exam stress?
options: A. It influences some students more strongly than others.
B. It helps every learner think more clearly.
C. It always disappears once the exam begins.
D. It only affects students who have not studied.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: 'stress does not affect everyone equally' → mức độ ảnh hưởng khác nhau ở mỗi người, nên A đúng. B trái ý (sợ hãi cản trở suy nghĩ); C và D không được nêu trong bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

How do exam results help teachers, according to paragraph 3?
options: A. They prove that grammar is always easier than reading.
B. They allow teachers to give far fewer lessons.
C. They reveal which topics need more teaching.
D. They remove the need for any future planning.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: kết quả cho thấy 'which topics have been understood and which need more attention' → C. A hiểu sai ví dụ về ngữ pháp/đọc (chỉ là một trường hợp minh họa); B và D trái ý vì bài nói kết quả giúp điều chỉnh và lên kế hoạch tốt hơn.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 4, one criticism of exams is that
options: A. they take too long to mark and return to students.
B. they cannot easily measure skills like creativity and speaking.
C. they are only ever used in written school subjects.
D. they make everyday lessons far too enjoyable.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: 'Skills such as creativity, teamwork, and speaking are difficult to measure in a written paper' → B. A không được nhắc; C và D không phải nội dung phê bình trong bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

The word 'captures' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
options: A. hides
B. forgets
C. repeats
D. shows
questions.explanation: 'a single test only captures a small part of what a student can do' — 'captures' nghĩa là nắm bắt/thể hiện được, gần với 'shows' → D. Các từ 'hides' (che giấu), 'forgets' (quên), 'repeats' (lặp lại) đều trái nghĩa hoặc không phù hợp ngữ cảnh.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

The word 'they' in paragraph 5 ("but they work best alongside other methods") refers to
options: A. exams
B. educators
C. projects
D. students
questions.explanation: Câu 'Exams still have an important role... but they work best alongside other methods' — 'they' nối tiếp chủ ngữ 'Exams' → A. 'Projects' mới là 'other methods' đứng sau nên không thể là chủ ngữ; 'educators' và 'students' không khớp mạch câu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What can be inferred about the writer's opinion of exams?
options: A. Exams should be removed from schools completely.
B. Written tests are the only fair way to measure ability.
C. Exams are useful but should be combined with other methods.
D. Teachers should ignore what exam results tell them.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 5 ủng hộ 'a balanced approach': kỳ thi vẫn quan trọng nhưng nên đi cùng dự án, thuyết trình, đánh giá liên tục → C. A và B là hai thái cực mà tác giả không đồng tình; D trái đoạn 3 (kết quả thi giúp giáo viên điều chỉnh).

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to the passage, all of the following are benefits of exams EXCEPT:
options: A. They can motivate students to study.
B. They measure creativity and teamwork accurately.
C. They show teachers which topics to review.
D. They give students a clear goal to aim for.
questions.explanation: A (đoạn 2), C (đoạn 3), D (đoạn 2) đều là lợi ích được nêu. Riêng B trái với đoạn 4: sáng tạo và làm việc nhóm 'difficult to measure', tức KHÔNG đo chính xác được → B là đáp án cho câu NGOẠI TRỪ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Fish milk is a long-established drink that has recently become fashionable again.
B. Fish milk is a manufactured substitute being studied to ease health and environmental problems.
C. Fish milk is a liquid taken directly from several species of fish.
D. Fish milk has already replaced cow's milk across much of the world.
questions.explanation: Cả bài mô tả sữa cá như một sản phẩm được chế tạo và đang được nghiên cứu như câu trả lời cho vấn đề dinh dưỡng và môi trường (đoạn 1, 3). A sai vì đây là sản phẩm mới, không phải thức uống lâu đời; C sai vì đoạn 1 nói rõ nó KHÔNG được lấy trực tiếp từ con vật mà được chế tạo từ protein và dầu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 2, what do manufacturers usually start with?
options: A. Whole fish that are caught especially for making the drink.
B. Milk that is collected from large mammals living in the sea.
C. Pieces of fish that would usually be thrown away as waste.
D. Plant oils that are blended with a small amount of fish.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 nói nhà sản xuất bắt đầu với những phần của con cá lẽ ra bị bỏ đi (phần vụn sau khi phi lê). A sai vì họ dùng phụ phẩm chứ không phải cá đánh bắt riêng; B sai vì sữa cá không hề được vắt từ động vật có vú.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 4, the word "off-putting" is closest in meaning to:
options: A. unpleasant
B. surprising
C. expensive
D. familiar
questions.explanation: "Off-putting" chỉ điều gây khó chịu, làm người ta không muốn dùng — ở đây là dư vị tanh khiến người thử thấy khó chịu, nên "unpleasant" đúng. "Surprising" và "familiar" không mang nghĩa tiêu cực về cảm giác vị giác.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 3, why is fish milk suitable for many people who avoid dairy?
options: A. It costs noticeably less than ordinary cow's milk.
B. It has a much stronger taste than cow's milk.
C. It can be kept for weeks without any refrigeration.
D. It contains none of the sugar that dairy milk has.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 nói nhiều người không tiêu hóa được lactose (loại đường trong sữa bò) nên tránh sữa, còn sữa cá thì không chứa lactose. A, B, C là các đặc điểm không được nêu như lý do phù hợp cho người tránh sữa.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

The passage states that fish milk is naturally rich in:
options: A. calcium along with vitamin D.
B. a range of natural plant proteins.
C. beneficial omega-3 fats that support good health.
D. natural sugars that boost energy.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 nêu sữa cá giàu axit béo omega-3, dưỡng chất liên quan đến sức khỏe tim và não. A không được nhắc tới; D sai vì bài nhấn mạnh sữa cá KHÔNG chứa lactose, không nói giàu đường.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 2, the word "These" (in "These are carefully cleaned...") refers to:
options: A. the consumers who dislike seafood.
B. the fillets that are sold in shops.
C. the natural sweeteners and stabilisers.
D. the leftover pieces of the fish.
questions.explanation: "These" nối lại với "parts of the fish that would otherwise be discarded... the trimmings" ngay câu trước, tức những phần cá thừa. C được nhắc sau đó ở khâu tái kết hợp, không phải thứ được làm sạch; B chỉ là mốc thời gian (sau khi cắt phi lê), không phải vật được làm sạch.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What did laboratory tests reveal about the protein in fish milk?
options: A. It is invariably lower than the protein in dairy.
B. It may match or go beyond the level found in dairy.
C. It breaks down and disappears while being stored.
D. It relies completely on the flavours that are added.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 nói hàm lượng protein của sữa cá có thể sánh ngang hoặc vượt sữa bò. A trái ngược trực tiếp; C nhầm lẫn — bài nói chất béo vẫn ổn định khi bảo quản, không phải protein biến mất.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about the future of fish milk?
options: A. Winning over shoppers may be harder than fixing the technology.
B. The technical problems will never be solved by scientists.
C. Consumers everywhere already prefer it to cow's milk.
D. Adding flavours has made no difference to its taste.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 nói các nhà nghiên cứu thừa nhận thuyết phục người mua có thể khó hơn giải quyết khó khăn kỹ thuật — hàm ý sự chấp nhận của người dùng là thách thức lớn hơn. B quá tuyệt đối; D trái với việc thêm vani/sô-cô-la khiến một số người không nhận ra khác biệt.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 5, all of the following are mentioned as possible uses of fish milk EXCEPT:
options: A. as an ingredient in foods such as yoghurt or sauces.
B. as a supplement for people short of omega-3.
C. as a feed given to farm animals such as cattle.
D. as a drink in places where dairy is hard to store.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 5 nêu các công dụng: thành phần trong sữa chua/nước sốt/món nướng (A), thực phẩm bổ sung omega-3 (B), và thức uống ở vùng khó bảo quản sữa (D). Việc làm thức ăn cho gia súc (C) hoàn toàn không được nhắc tới, nên là đáp án cho câu NGOẠI TRỪ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What broader point does the final paragraph make?
options: A. Fish milk is certain to dominate supermarkets very soon.
B. Tomorrow's meals might be made from long-overlooked sources.
C. Traditional dairy farming should be banned immediately.
D. Consumers will never accept any milk alternative.
questions.explanation: Câu cuối nói nghiên cứu phản ánh chuyển dịch tư duy rằng thực phẩm tương lai có thể đến từ những nguồn ta đã bỏ qua từ lâu — đúng với B. A quá chắc chắn ("whether or not it ever reaches" cho thấy chưa chắc); C và D là những khẳng định cực đoan không có trong bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What is the writer's main purpose in the passage?
options: A. To prove that digital technology has revolutionised education beyond any doubt.
B. To offer a balanced assessment of technology's effects across several dimensions.
C. To warn schools firmly against adopting digital tools at all.
D. To describe in detail how a single flipped classroom operates.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1 nêu rõ tác giả muốn "cân nhắc các chiều kích với nhau" và khẳng định ảnh hưởng "không hoàn toàn tích cực cũng chẳng hoàn toàn tiêu cực" — tức một đánh giá cân bằng, nên B đúng. A và C sai vì cực đoan một chiều (thuần ca ngợi / thuần bác bỏ), còn D chỉ là một chi tiết nhỏ chứ không phải mục đích toàn bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to paragraph 2, what was personalised learning like before adaptive software became common?
options: A. It was widely available to learners in the most remote areas.
B. It depended chiefly on the instantaneous feedback of algorithms.
C. It was mostly reserved for students who could pay for private tutoring.
D. It forced all learners to progress at exactly the same pace.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 viết cá nhân hóa "từng là đặc quyền của những học sinh có đủ điều kiện thuê gia sư riêng", khớp với C. A trái ngược (không hề rộng rãi), B nhầm sang đặc điểm của phần mềm hiện nay, còn D mô tả điều ngược với ý "điều chỉnh theo tốc độ từng cá nhân".

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 4, the word "thrift" is closest in meaning to:
options: A. carefulness in the way money is spent
B. a willingness to give money away freely
C. a large amount of financial investment
D. an unexpected and lasting difficulty
questions.explanation: "Thrift" nghĩa là sự tiết kiệm, chi tiêu cẩn thận — ở đây chỉ khoản tiết kiệm khi nhân bản sách số gần như miễn phí, nên A đúng. B trái nghĩa (hào phóng cho đi), C và D đi ngược ngữ cảnh vì câu ngay sau đó mới nói tới khoản chi lớn ("substantial outlay").

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What characterises the "flipped classroom" as described in paragraph 3?
options: A. Learners attend all their lectures on distant elite campuses.
B. Learners take in fresh content beforehand and use lessons for practice.
C. Teachers deliver every part of the course through recorded videos.
D. Classroom sessions are done away with in favour of online chats.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 nói lớp đảo ngược cho học sinh "tiếp thu kiến thức mới ở nhà qua bài giảng ghi hình và dành thời gian trên lớp cho thảo luận và giải quyết vấn đề", khớp B. A mô tả khóa trực tuyến ở câu khác; C và D thổi phồng thành "mọi phần" hay "xóa bỏ lớp học" — không đúng vì giờ trên lớp vẫn được giữ cho thảo luận.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What does the passage imply about the teacher's role under these new methods?
options: A. It becomes largely unnecessary once the lessons are recorded.
B. It is reduced to marking student essays more quickly than before.
C. It grows heavier because online class sizes keep increasing.
D. It moves from simply delivering information to guiding students where they struggle.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 viết sự sắp xếp lại "giải phóng giáo viên khỏi vai trò chỉ là người thuyết giảng, biến họ thành người hướng dẫn can thiệp đúng chỗ khi có bối rối", nên D đúng. A sai vì bài không nói giáo viên trở nên thừa; B và C là chi tiết bị bóp méo, không được đề cập.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What paradox concerning cost does the passage identify?
options: A. Digital resources are cheap to copy, yet printed books stay more popular.
B. A tool celebrated for broadening access can deepen inequality when adopted unevenly.
C. Wealthy institutions end up spending far less than poorer ones on technology.
D. Open educational resources cost more to produce than printed textbooks do.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 nêu rõ nghịch lý: công nghệ "được ca ngợi vì mở rộng tiếp cận" nhưng "nếu phân bổ không đồng đều" có thể "khoét sâu chính khoảng cách", khớp B. A, C, D đều là những suy diễn không có trong bài và trái với lập luận (cơ sở nghèo mới chật vật, sao chép số gần như miễn phí).

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 4, the word "them" (in "struggle to furnish them") refers to:
options: A. families who used to buy printed volumes
B. open educational resources and digital textbooks
C. dependable devices, strong networks and regular software updates
D. institutions located in less affluent regions
questions.explanation: Câu viết: "Thiết bị đáng tin cậy, mạng lưới ổn định và các bản cập nhật... các cơ sở... chật vật để trang bị chúng (them)". Vậy "them" chỉ các thứ vừa liệt kê — C đúng. D là chủ ngữ thực hiện hành động "furnish" chứ không phải đối tượng; A và B thuộc câu trước, không phải thứ được "trang bị".

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What can be inferred about the new occupations mentioned in paragraph 5?
options: A. They have already completely replaced all traditional teaching roles.
B. They had existed long before digital technology entered classrooms.
C. They are generally disliked by most younger workers today.
D. They came into being as a direct result of technological change in education.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 5 nói "tự động hóa đã khai sinh những nghề hoàn toàn mới... hầu như chưa tồn tại một thế hệ trước" — tức chúng xuất hiện do thay đổi công nghệ, nên D đúng. B mâu thuẫn trực tiếp với "chưa tồn tại một thế hệ trước"; A quá tuyệt đối (bài nói sự thay thế vẫn chưa chắc chắn); C không được đề cập.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

How would the writer's overall attitude towards digital technology in education best be described?
options: A. cautious and even-handed
B. wholeheartedly optimistic
C. deeply pessimistic
D. completely indifferent
questions.explanation: Suốt bài tác giả công nhận lợi ích nhưng luôn kèm điều kiện và cảnh báo ("lợi ích mang tính điều kiện chứ không tự động", "không phải hào hứng thiếu phê phán cũng chẳng phải kháng cự"), nên thái độ là thận trọng, công tâm — A đúng. B và C đều là cực đoan một chiều; D sai vì bài rõ ràng có quan tâm và đánh giá có chủ đích.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

The passage mentions all of the following as effects of digital technology EXCEPT:
options: A. faster feedback on students' written work
B. the appearance of new kinds of educational jobs
C. a guaranteed reduction in overall educational costs
D. wider access to lectures for learners in remote areas
questions.explanation: A (phản hồi tức thì, đoạn 2), B (nghề mới, đoạn 5) và D (tiếp cận từ vùng xa, đoạn 3) đều được nêu rõ. Riêng C sai vì bài nhấn mạnh chi phí là "mơ hồ" và tiết kiệm chỉ xảy ra "trong điều kiện phù hợp", không hề "chắc chắn" — nên đây là phương án ngoại trừ cần chọn.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: A. The dollar is about to be replaced by the euro and the Chinese renminbi.
B. The United States deliberately manipulates the dollar in order to harm poorer nations.
C. The dollar's global role and its shifting value shape economies far beyond America, making it both useful and risky.
D. Central banks around the world should stop holding any of their reserves in dollars.
questions.explanation: Cả bài xoay quanh vai trò toàn cầu của đồng đô la và cách dao động giá trị của nó ảnh hưởng tới nhiều nền kinh tế, kết lại là 'vừa tiện lợi vừa là điểm yếu' — trùng với C. A và D là những khẳng định tuyệt đối mà đoạn cuối bác bỏ (bàn về sự cáo chung là 'quá sớm'); B gán ý 'cố tình thao túng' mà bài không nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to the passage, which of the following is one reason so many countries rely on the dollar?
options: A. Enormous amounts of dollar assets can be traded without causing prices to swing sharply.
B. The United States compels its trading partners to settle all accounts in dollars.
C. The American economy now produces a steadily growing share of world output.
D. Rival currencies are legally forbidden from being used in international trade.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 nêu 'liquidity' (thanh khoản): thị trường đô la sâu đến mức mua bán khoản lớn không làm giá biến động mạnh — chính là A. C trái với bài ('tỷ trọng của Mỹ dần suy giảm'); B và D bịa ra sự ép buộc/cấm đoán mà bài không đề cập.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What does the passage say happens when the dollar depreciates against other currencies?
options: A. American exports become more expensive abroad and therefore fall.
B. US products become more affordable to overseas customers, which usually lifts exports.
C. Imported goods immediately become cheaper for American consumers.
D. The American trade deficit widens sharply overnight.
questions.explanation: Quan hệ nhân–quả ở đoạn 3: đô la yếu → hàng Mỹ rẻ hơn với người mua ngoài → kích thích xuất khẩu (B). A đảo ngược (đắt hơn → giảm là sai vì đô la yếu làm hàng RẺ hơn). C sai vì đô la yếu khiến hàng nhập ĐẮT hơn với người Mỹ; D sai vì bài nói xu hướng THU HẸP thâm hụt.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

According to the passage, a strengthening dollar affects developing countries that borrow in dollars by
options: A. reducing the amount they must repay when measured in their local currencies.
B. encouraging foreign investors to pour fresh capital into their markets.
C. lowering the cost of the oil and food that these countries import.
D. making their debts heavier, because paying back each dollar now demands more local money.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 nói đô la tăng giá 'thổi phồng gánh nặng thực của các khoản nợ' vì mỗi đô la trả nợ tốn nhiều nội tệ hơn — đúng D. A đảo ngược; B sai vì vốn CHẢY RA khỏi thị trường mới nổi về Mỹ; C sai vì hàng nhập ĐẮT hơn khi... thực ra bài nói khi đô la mạnh thì hàng nhập cũng đắt hơn với các nền kinh tế đó, không phải rẻ đi.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 5, the word 'dwarfed' is closest in meaning to
options: A. made to seem small by comparison.
B. delayed for a considerable period of time.
C. explained in careful and thorough detail.
D. divided up and shared among many parties.
questions.explanation: Câu nói một vụ mùa thất bát hay khủng hoảng nhỏ có thể bị 'dwarfed' bởi thay đổi chính sách tiền tệ Mỹ — nghĩa là bị lu mờ, trở nên nhỏ bé khi so sánh (A). Các phương án B, C, D không khớp nghĩa 'lu mờ/bị áp đảo về quy mô'.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

In paragraph 4, the word 'they' in the phrase 'when they can least afford it' refers to
options: A. the higher returns that capital seeks.
B. the emerging markets losing funds.
C. the imported commodities that grow costlier.
D. the American investors moving their money.
questions.explanation: Câu 'draining funds from emerging markets precisely when they can least afford it' — 'they' chỉ chính 'emerging markets' (các thị trường mới nổi) đang bị rút vốn (B). A, C, D không phải chủ thể 'ít có khả năng chịu đựng' việc mất vốn.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

It can be inferred that some governments hold euros, gold, or the renminbi in their reserves because they
options: A. expect the dollar to lose all of its value within a few years.
B. are legally required to spread their reserves across many currencies.
C. wish to reduce their exposure to decisions made by American policymakers.
D. find these assets far easier to buy and sell than dollar assets.
questions.explanation: Việc đa dạng hóa đứng ngay sau lời than phiền rằng quyết định của Fed dội tới mọi nơi bất kể điều kiện địa phương → suy ra họ muốn bớt lệ thuộc vào chính sách Mỹ (C). A quá tuyệt đối và bị đoạn cuối bác; B bịa ràng buộc pháp lý; D trái với việc bài nhấn mạnh thanh khoản vượt trội của đô la.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

What can be inferred about the author's view of predictions that the dollar will soon collapse?
options: A. The author is convinced such a collapse will occur within the coming decade.
B. The author believes the renminbi has already overtaken the dollar.
C. The author thinks the dollar's role ended once America's output share fell.
D. The author regards such predictions as repeatedly made yet so far unfounded.
questions.explanation: Đoạn cuối: bàn về sự cáo chung của đô la 'đã lưu hành suốt nhiều thập kỷ' và hiện 'phần lớn vẫn còn quá sớm' → tác giả coi các dự đoán này lặp đi lặp lại nhưng chưa thành hiện thực (D). A, B, C mâu thuẫn trực tiếp với luận điểm rằng đô la vẫn giữ vị thế thống trị.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

How would you best describe the author's overall attitude towards the dollar-centred system?
options: A. Balanced, acknowledging both its advantages and its dangers.
B. Enthusiastic, praising it as flawless and sure to last forever.
C. Hostile, calling openly for its immediate abolition.
D. Indifferent, treating it as unimportant to ordinary people.
questions.explanation: Tác giả vừa nêu lợi thế (thanh khoản, niềm tin, tiện lợi) vừa nêu rủi ro (nợ, cú sốc chính sách, sự phụ thuộc), khép lại bằng 'vừa tiện lợi vừa là điểm yếu' → thái độ cân bằng (A). B quá tán dương, C quá thù địch, D sai vì bài nhấn mạnh tác động lên 'đời sống thường nhật'.

questions.content:
reading — Passage

The passage mentions all of the following as reasons for the dollar's dominance EXCEPT
options: A. the depth and liquidity of dollar-denominated markets.
B. a binding international treaty that requires countries to use it.
C. trust in American institutions and a record of never defaulting.
D. the network effect created by the currency's widespread use.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 liệt kê ba lý do: niềm tin (C), thanh khoản (A) và quán tính/hiệu ứng mạng lưới (D). Bài KHÔNG hề nói tới một hiệp ước ràng buộc nào — B là điều không được nêu, nên đó là đáp án cho câu NGOẠI TRỪ.
